findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never validates the grant shortcut (inverted condition and wrong substring bounds)
findings.body: In the newly added isAccessTokenId matcher, the line `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is wrong twice: (1) the condition is inverted — it returns false (no match) when the grant shortcut *equals* the expected value, i.e. it would reject a correct token ID and accept an incorrect one; (2) the bounds are wrong — in an encoded token ID like `onrtac:<uuid>` the 2-char grant shortcut sits at indexes 4-5, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`; `substring(3, 5)` yields e.g. "ta" for `onrtac`. As written the check can essentially never fire, so the matcher degenerates to a UUID check on the part after the colon. Consequence: all updated event assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass regardless of which grant type is actually encoded in the token ID, so the integration-level verification of this PR's main feature is vacuous — a grant flow that forgets to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE (and thus encodes "na") or encodes the wrong shortcut would go completely undetected.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: The AccessTokenContext constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` — the third check repeats grantType instead of checking rawTokenId. As a result a null rawTokenId is silently accepted, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId would then produce a token ID ending in `...:null` instead of failing fast. The line should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes due to NullPointerException from uninitialized sessionFactory, not the intended validation error
findings.body: The test's before() method calls factory.init(null) and sets the shortcut maps directly, but never calls postInit(), so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory remains null. When getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678") encounters the unregistered "ac" shortcut, getGrantTypeByShortcut() enters its lazy-refresh branch and calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...), which throws a NullPointerException. The test catches generic RuntimeException, so it passes for the wrong reason and does not verify the intended IllegalArgumentException("Unknown value 'ac' for grant type"). If decoding stopped rejecting unknown shortcuts, this test would not necessarily catch it. It should catch IllegalArgumentException specifically (and assert the message), so the intended behavior is actually verified.

findings.title: getShortcut() javadoc says "3-letters shortcut" but the decoder requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The javadoc for the new getShortcut() method says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants". However, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId assumes the grant shortcut is exactly 2 characters: it requires a 6-character context prefix and parses it as 2 (session type) + 2 (token type) + 2 (grant type). All built-in grants added in this PR return 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "ro", ...). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implemented following this javadoc with a 3-letter shortcut would emit token IDs that the decoder then rejects as malformed. The javadoc should state that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and unique across grants.
